summary: Backend-only test of iter-40 fix (shared yolov8s zoom for fast-model cameras + multi-scale early stop + fail-closed person rule). All requested regression files: 119/119 passed. Live-service E2E tests/zoom_real_yolo_check.py: 'RESULT: PASS [True, True]' (dog 0 events, person 1 event, fast tier). Added tests/test_iter41_zoom_edges.py with 24 new edge-case tests (scripted early stop / best-per-class / None handling, off-frame no inference, shared zoom lock serialises concurrent inference across 2 fast detectors x 3 threads (peak concurrency 1), accurate camera no lock, missing yolov8s fallback, Track.person_conf maths incl. via CentroidTracker.update, _animal_on_zoom boundaries at exactly 0.25 / 0.70, exception & unknown-track fail-open, full-res box scaling, two real fast detectors zooming user dogs concurrently, 2x upscaled user dog) — 24/24 pass. Exploratory real-model check: night_person shrunk to 0.6/0.4/0.3 scale (down to 16x38 px, frame conf 0.54) still zooms as person 0.90 on yolov8s with looks=1 on both tiers, so the fail-closed rule did not drop a genuine small person in these checks. Full suite (minus tests/real): 469 passed, 2 skipped; the only failures (1 F + 16 E) are in test_service_api.py, caused by test_engine.py leaving requests.post patched; test_service_api.py passes 20/20 when run on its own.

minor.issue: test_engine.py lines 125/166/432 assign whatsapp.requests.post = fake_post without restoring it. whatsapp.requests is the global requests module, so later test_service_api.py tests in the same run get the fake response (login wrong password -> 200, 'R' object has no attribute ...). This existed before this change. Use monkeypatch.setattr.

action_items: Optional: make test_engine.py restore whatsapp.requests.post (monkeypatch) so the full suite runs clean in one pytest invocation
Optional: preload the shared yolov8s zoom model in the background at engine start on fast-tier PCs. Right now the first zoom loads it (~5 s) inside the frame loop, holding _ZOOM_LOCK.
critical_code_review_comments: engine._animal_on_zoom: tr.zoom_person is a SUM over looks, so several weak noise looks (e.g. 0.12+0.12+0.02) add up past ZOOM_PERSON_MIN=0.25 and let a hesitant full-frame person through. test_noise_person_scores_sum_over_looks documents this. If that is not intended, use max (or the mean) of the zoomed person scores.

detector.zoom_model_for: if yolov8s.pt exists but fails to load (corrupt file or partial update), YOLO() raises every time and the load is retried on every zoom while holding _ZOOM_LOCK. Every look then goes through the exception path, which fails open, so animals would alert again. Cache the failure, fall back to the camera's own model, and log it once.

Fast-tier CPU cost: each person track near the line gets up to 3 yolov8s looks per ZOOM_EVERY_S, serialised across all fast cameras by one lock. On a slow multi-camera PC this can back up the frame loop. Consider a non-blocking acquire or a per-second zoom budget.

second_opinion scales (1.5,320) and (1.5,640) use the same crop. That is fine, but stopping as soon as an animal is 'clear' means a person who briefly looks dog-like on the 320 look never gets the 640 look. Given the user's no-animal requirement this is an acceptable bias.

success_rate.backend: 100% of feature tests (119 regression + 24 new + live E2E); full suite 469 passed, 17 test_service_api.py tests failing only because test_engine.py leaks a patched requests.post (pass when run alone)
